correctness.rationale: Hall local finiteness makes every marked finite-tuple subgroup finite. Evaluation F_V(n)-><g_i> has a finite-index normal kernel, and equal kernels are equivalent to an isomorphism of the marked finite subgroups. Rzepecki/Hall inner ultrahomogeneity realizes it by conjugation, while all group automorphisms preserve words. Every finite quotient embeds by Hall universality. Abelian exponent-m relatively free group is (Z/m)^n; prime-power subgroup count is exactly Birkhoff rectangular formula. A Gaussian coefficient has size p^{k(N-k)} up to fixed p constant, with subgroup-type exponent sum r_i(n-r_i), giving the claimed O(log n) remainder.

evidence: Rzepecki proves the stronger finite-partial-isomorphism extension by inner conjugation for Hall group. A tuple marked isomorphism is a direct special case. Hall embeds every finite marked group.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The original broad group-homogeneity theorem directly entails all tuple kernel classes, regardless of variety; narrowing to word-law strata cannot avoid this implication.

evidence: Combine prior inner ultrahomogeneity and the standard free-group presentation of a tuple: two tuples have same kernel iff they define a marked subgroup isomorphism; existing Birkhoff count gives all abelian exponent-m orbit counts. The asymptotic is the standard p^{k(n-k)} degree bound in the same formula.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: All quantified conclusions, including full versus inner Aut agreement and m^{n^2/4+o(n^2)} growth, are routine consequences of the two checked prior facts. Different terminology/numeric encoding does not constitute an original theorem.

evidence: The defining inner ultrahomogeneity means exactly that finite marked tuples with the same group-word relations are conjugate; equality of relations is equality of kernels of the marked free evaluation.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The purported normal-subgroup orbit parametrization is not a mathematically new classification relative to the older quantifier-free-type/marked subgroup statement: it is its canonical re-expression.

evidence: The displayed S_{a,n}(p) is literally the classical Birkhoff formula for rectangular subgroup types. For prime m it is the classical Gaussian/Galois number.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Once one reinterprets the marked orbit as a subgroup, no new enumeration occurs: the numeric profile already exists in finite abelian subgroup tables.

originality.rationale: Decisive prior implication: Hall/Rzepecki inner ultrahomogeneity makes finite marked-subgroup isomorphisms inner-conjugate, which is exactly equality of relatively free word kernels; existing Birkhoff formula and Gaussian estimates then supply the rest.
residual_risks: Source proves exact mathematical identities, but their claimed distinct original contribution is directly covered by structural prior and classical tables.
Does not assert full Gamma^n has finitely many orbits; unbounded element orders imply infinite overall orbit set.
No false proof; rejection is originality/value only.
